sections.title: In the Kitchen
sections.content: Cooking is mostly regular -ar verbs, which you can already build: cocinar, cortar, preparar, mezclar. Two of the useful ones change their stem the way 'querer' does — 'probar' becomes 'prueba' and 'calentar' becomes 'calienta' — so learn those two shapes as they come.

items.spanish: Tenemos tortillas, pollo, queso, tomates y salsa.
items.english: We have tortillas, chicken, cheese, tomatoes and sauce.

items.spanish: Solo necesita un poco más de sal.
items.english: It just needs a little more salt.

items.spanish: Meg calienta las tortillas y Lauren prepara la mesa.
items.english: Meg heats the tortillas and Lauren sets the table.

sections.content: 'La sal' is one of the feminine words that does not end in -a, and 'el plato' means both the plate and the dish you serve on it — 'los platos típicos de mi país' is the food, not the crockery.
